answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on shared work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit proves a claim was fabricated. Splitting one operator across a nebula of accounts does not multiply influence for free: every account must lock more capital, and each false report risks forfeiture. A prism of independent auditors can compare evidence, while shale-like persistence of the stake makes rapid identity churn costly.
